summary: Iteration 14: tested the overview dashboard, client links/public branding, the per-client PWA manifest/icons and tenant isolation, plus a static review of the deploy package. Backend: new pytest file with 20 tests, all passing (public branding/logo/manifest incl. 404s, square PNG icons at 180/192/512, original logo <=256, slug 422/409, set/clear slug, unauth 401, client user sees only own device, non-simulated device offline, device create/delete works with dynsec as a no-op). test_multitenant.py regression passed 14/14. Frontend at 390x844, all checked flows PASS: (1) ?klient=kowalski gives the Kowalski logo, title 'Kowalski Wentylacja', amber theme, and the manifest link, apple-touch-icon and document.title switch; the slug is kept in localStorage across a reload; ?klient=nieistnieje gives default branding and the key is removed. (2) Superadmin sees nav-overview; cards are sorted alarms-first (chlodnia-01 with chamber 2 threshold lowered shows overview-alarms badge '1' and a red cell); the non-simulated TEST device shows 'offline' plus waiting text; tapping a card selects the device, opens Komory and switches branding. (3) BrandEditor: invalid slug toast, duplicate 'kowalski' toast 'Ten link jest już zajęty', save shows brand-link https://<host>/?klient=test-ui-mp, copy puts the right URL on the clipboard, clearing hides the link. (4) Kowalski operator sees overview with only Kowalski devices; Marco Polo operator (1 device) has no nav-overview and gets the green/default branding. Regression for device switching, Dane charts, Ustawienia and the fleet card: OK. Deploy static review found one blocking problem: Mosquitto cannot read the Caddy TLS key.

minor.issue: This legacy pre-multitenant suite is stale (18 failures: old endpoints like /usage/daily and /simulator/toggle, plus single-device state assumptions). These are not app regressions; the suite should be deleted or rewritten.

issues: The DevicePicker and status bar ('Sterownik offline') above the overview still describe the currently selected device. That is confusing on a fleet-wide screen; hide them in the overview view or show fleet totals instead.
6-chamber devices use a 5-column grid, so K6 wraps alone onto a second row. Use 3 or 6 columns (e.g. cols = n<=5 ? n : Math.ceil(n/2)).
Mini cells show the CO2 number without a unit (e.g. '2217'). Add 'ppm' or a CO2 label.

Devices are sorted by name, so 'TEST_offline' came before 'Tuczarnia A' and a user with no saved device landed on an offline device ('waiting for data'). Prefer the first online device as the default.

action_items: CRITICAL (deploy): Mosquitto 2.x drops privileges to the 'mosquitto' user before it loads the TLS cert/key, and Caddy stores private keys as root 0600 in caddy_data. The 8883 listener will therefore fail with 'Unable to load server key file'. Fix in the mosquitto command: copy the cert and key into /mosquitto/certs/, chown mosquitto:mosquitto, chmod 600, then point certfile/keyfile in mosquitto.conf.tpl at /mosquitto/certs/. The weekly restart cron then re-copies the renewed cert.

Deploy doc step 6: 'docker compose up -d web backend mongo' also starts mosquitto, because backend has depends_on: mosquitto. Mosquitto then restart-loops until Caddy has the cert. This is harmless but contradicts the doc; either remove mosquitto from backend depends_on or reword step 6/7.

Deploy: the cert path is hardcoded to the Let's Encrypt issuer directory (acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org-directory). If Caddy falls back to ZeroSSL, the path changes (acme.zerossl.com-v2-dv90). Mention this in 'Problemy', or pin the issuer in the Caddyfile (tls { issuer acme }).
Overview UX: hide the device picker/status bar in the overview, and fix the 6-chamber grid and the CO2 unit (see design_issues).
Optional: on the login screen, a ?klient= value with an invalid format (e.g. ?klient=BAD) is ignored and the previously stored slug's branding stays. Decide whether it should clear the stored slug.
Delete or rewrite the stale backend/tests/test_auth_security.py.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py patch_client: slug uniqueness is only checked in app code (find_one, then update), so there is a race. Add a unique partial index on clients.slug (partialFilterExpression slug: {$gt: ''}).
server.py public_logo: size values other than 180/192/512 silently return the original image. Fine, but a 422 would be clearer.

dynsec_add_device sends deleteClient before createClient, so the first provisioning returns an error entry for the delete. This is harmless (dynsec processes commands independently), but the backend never reads the $CONTROL/dynamic-security/v1/response topic, so provisioning failures are invisible. Consider subscribing and logging errors.
Devices that exist before MQTT_DYNSEC=1 is enabled (e.g. after a DB restore/migration) never get broker accounts. Consider a startup reconcile or a 'reprovision' button.
App.js usePublicBrand: .catch removes brand_slug on any error, including network/5xx. Only remove it on a 404.
Cookies are SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned. That works on the same-origin VPS behind HTTPS; on the VPS, SameSite=Lax would be the stricter choice.

Playwright note: on the Dane view, a normal click on nav-settings timed out at 'scrolling into view' although elementFromPoint returns the button and force-click works. This looks like a tooling quirk with fixed nav plus live charts, not a user-facing bug.

rca of the issue: Mosquitto TLS: since 2.0, mosquitto reads cert/key files after dropping root privileges (see mosquitto.org/documentation/migrating-to-2-0). Caddy writes its ACME private keys with mode 0600 owned by root in /data (mounted read-only at /caddy). The mosquitto user therefore cannot open the keyfile and the broker exits. The docker-entrypoint chown only covers /mosquitto, not /caddy. Mitigation: copy and chown the cert/key into /mosquitto/certs in the compose command before exec mosquitto.
